lab_questions.title: Practical SQL Evaluation
lab_questions.description: Evaluate candidates on their practical SQL skills across various domains.

tasks.title: E-Commerce: Top 3 Customers by Total Spend
tasks.description: Given two tables, `customers` (id, name, email) and `orders` (id, customer_id, amount, order_date), write a SQL query to retrieve the names and emails of the top 3 customers who have spent the most in total. The result should include `name`, `email`, and `total_spent`.

solution.query.sql: SELECT c.name, c.email, SUM(o.amount) as total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.email ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 3;

tasks.title: HR: Second Highest Salary per Department
tasks.description: Given two tables, `employees` (id, name, salary, department_id) and `departments` (id, name), write a SQL query to find the employee with the second highest salary in each department. Use Window Functions. Output should be `department_name`, `employee_name`, and `salary`.

solution.query.sql: WITH RankedSalaries AS (SELECT d.name as department_name, e.name as employee_name, e.salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY e.department_id ORDER BY e.salary DESC) as rn FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id) SELECT department_name, employee_name, salary FROM RankedSalaries WHERE rn = 2;

tasks.title: Finance: 7-Day Rolling Average of Transactions
tasks.description: Given a table `transactions` (transaction_id, amount, transaction_date), write a SQL query to calculate the 7-day rolling average of total transaction amounts for each day. The result should include `transaction_date` and `rolling_avg`.

solution.query.sql: WITH daily_totals AS (SELECT transaction_date, SUM(amount) AS daily_total FROM transactions GROUP BY transaction_date) SELECT transaction_date, AVG(daily_total) OVER (ORDER BY transaction_date ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS rolling_avg FROM daily_totals ORDER BY transaction_date;

tasks.title: Sales: Products with No Sales in 6 Months
tasks.description: Given two tables, `products` (id, name, category) and `sales` (id, product_id, sale_date, quantity), write a SQL query to identify all products that have not been sold in the last 6 months from the current date. Include `product_id` and `product_name`.

solution.query.sql: SELECT p.id as product_id, p.name as product_name FROM products p LEFT JOIN sales s ON p.id = s.product_id AND s.sale_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 months' WHERE s.id IS NULL;

tasks.title: Social Media: Users Who Liked All Posts by a Specific User
tasks.description: Given tables `users` (id, username), `posts` (id, author_id, content), and `likes` (user_id, post_id), write a query to find the usernames of all users who have liked EVERY single post created by the user with username 'influencer_x'.

solution.query.sql: SELECT u.username FROM users u JOIN likes l ON u.id = l.user_id JOIN posts p ON l.post_id = p.id WHERE p.author_id = (SELECT id FROM users WHERE username = 'influencer_x') GROUP BY u.id, u.username HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts WHERE author_id = (SELECT id FROM users WHERE username = 'influencer_x'));

tasks.title: Healthcare: Patients with Multiple Visits in a Month
tasks.description: Given two tables, `patients` (id, name) and `visits` (id, patient_id, visit_date), write a SQL query to find the names of patients who have visited more than once in November 2023. Include `name` and `visit_count`.

solution.query.sql: SELECT p.name, COUNT(v.id) as visit_count FROM patients p JOIN visits v ON p.id = v.patient_id WHERE v.visit_date >= '2023-11-01' AND v.visit_date <= '2023-11-30' GROUP BY p.id, p.name HAVING COUNT(v.id) > 1;

tasks.title: Education: Students with Average Grade Above 80
tasks.description: Given two tables, `students` (id, name) and `grades` (id, student_id, course, grade), write a SQL query to retrieve the names of students whose average grade across all courses is strictly greater than 80. Include `name` and `avg_grade`.

solution.query.sql: SELECT s.name, AVG(g.grade) as avg_grade FROM students s JOIN grades g ON s.id = g.student_id GROUP BY s.id, s.name HAVING AVG(g.grade) > 80;
